title: Microbuffer staffing, runway & sliding price anchors
content:
Purpose: quick spreadsheet-style working note to map a 6-month runway for microbuffer staffing (contractor + perm mix), embed sliding price anchors across three customer tiers, and simulate price sensitivity under two token-intensity scenarios. Intended as a working input for FY27 sprint-level hiring decisions and near-term slab/spot price gating.

Summary headline: Keep a 10–15% microbuffer in available GPU-week equivalent while preserving a 6–8% margin at moderate token-intensity. If high token-intensity persists, trigger hiring cadence OR move 12% of mid-size customers to tiered surge pricing.

ASSUMPTIONS (source notes):
- Baseline throughput demand growth: +8% month-over-month aggregate across hosted API.
- Token intensity buckets: Low (0.7x baseline), Mid (1.0x baseline), High (1.6x baseline).
- GPU-week equivalency: 1 perm engineer = 0.02 GPU-weeks for on-call & ops capacity; 1 contractor = 0.01 GPU-weeks.
- Average cost per GPU-week (blended): $1,900. Operational cost per perm head: $18k/month fully-loaded; contractor fully-loaded: $9k/month.
- Target microbuffer: 10–15% of provisioned GPU-weeks to handle spikes.

Quick table: 6-month sprint runway view (columns = months May->Oct 2026)

| Item                        | May   | Jun   | Jul   | Aug   | Sep   | Oct   | Notes |
|-----------------------------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|
| Forecasted token demand (B) | 1.00  | 1.08  | 1.17  | 1.26  | 1.36  | 1.47  | scaled by growth assumption |
| Provisioned GPU-weeks       | 1,240 | 1,260 | 1,300 | 1,350 | 1,400 | 1,480 | baseline + planned bursts |
| Microbuffer (10%)           | 124   | 126   | 130   | 135   | 140   | 148   | target reserve capacity |
| Perm hires (engineers)     | 2     | 0     | 1     | 0     | 1     | 0     | hiring cadence to meet SLOs |
| Contractors (ops)          | 3     | 2     | 2     | 2     | 2     | 1     | short-term smoothing |
| Blended headcount cost ($k)| 72    | 54    | 60    | 54    | 60    | 36    | monthly fully-loaded est. |
| Monthly GPU cost ($k)      | 2,356 | 2,397 | 2,473 | 2,568 | 2,664 | 2,814 | provisioned * $1.9k/GW |
| Gross margin w/ current price (%) | 12.5 | 11.9 | 11.3 | 10.8 | 10.2 | 9.7 | without price adjustment |

Pricing sensitivity: sliding price anchors (three-tier model)
- Tier A (Enterprise SLA): base price multiplier = 1.00, can be adjusted by +5% during persistent high-intensity (>1.4x baseline demand)
- Tier B (Mid-market): base multiplier = 0.85, soft anchor to shift 8–12% of customers up to surge band when microbuffer <12%
- Tier C (Developer/PLG): base multiplier = 0.6, elastic; active throttle + credits for burst customers

Scenario sims (output summary):
- Mid demand (1.0x): If prices unchanged, runway margin drifts -2.8 p.p. across 6 months. Hiring plan above keeps latency SLOs but reduces cushion to microbuffer ≈10% by Oct.
- High demand (1.6x): Without price action, margin falls below 0 by Sep. Options: (A) escalate Tier B by +8% (projected recover +3.4 p.p.), (B) trigger hiring ramp (+4 perm hires across Jul-Aug, cost +$72k/mo) yields margin recover +2.6 p.p. but burns runway faster.
- Low demand (0.7x): Opportunity to defer 2 contractors and run cost-savings exercise; possible promotional credits to keep PLG stickiness.

Elasticity check: small sample of customers indicates price elasticity roughly -1.3 for Tier C, -0.6 for Tier B, and -0.2 for Tier A for transient token price moves. Use conservative elasticity of -0.8 when estimating revenue response to anchor changes.

Trigger rules (operational):
- If microbuffer < 11% for 2 consecutive measurement windows (weekly), auto-escalate Tier B anchor by +5% and open 1 perm hiring req for infra SRE.
- If realized token intensity >1.4x baseline for 3 weeks, open emergency budget to convert 2 contractors -> perm (retention) and enable Tier A emergency uplift (+5%).
- If margin <5% for a month, pause non-essential hiring and run 30-day cost-reduction scrub focused on GPU mix (move 7% workload to quantized variants).

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Finance: revisit blended GPU-week cost estimate with infra procurement (Ethan) and update sheet.
- Growth: identify top-25 PLG customers by token spikes to assess surge pricing friction (Ava).
- People Ops: prepare fast-track hiring sheet for 0–4 perm SRE hires and contractor conversion costs (Priya).
- Product: quick eval of prefix-cache improvements that would lower token intensity for top-cores (Miguel).

Notes & open questions:
- Need a small A/B to test Tier B +5% on a 10-customer sample to estimate real uptake; track churn risk weekly.
- Verify the contractor -> perm conversion time (recruiting lead time obs: 6–9 weeks).
- Confirm regulatory constraints for regional price differentiation (EMEA vs NA).

Bottom line (working): keep strategic flexibility: use layered levers (price anchors + microbuffer + hiring cadence) rather than a single blunt response. This sheet is a live model; update costs weekly and re-run high-demand scenario immediately if token intensity crosses 1.3x sustained."
